- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (positive sentiment > 0.10) — model tends to overshoot after spikes.
- Underestimate prices in bearish sentiment (negative sentiment < -0.10) — model fails to capture downward momentum.
- Lag in price correction: model often delays mean reversion, especially after strong sentiment shifts.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term sentiment swings — sentiment volatility should not trigger large forecast adjustments.
- For 30-day horizon, model overestimates in early periods after price spikes, then underestimates in late periods — adjust for asymmetric decay.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overforecast — reduce forecast by 2–5% in such cases.
- If sentiment turns sharply positive after a dip, model often fails to fully capture the rally — add 3–7% buffer to forecast.
